explanation:
Work through the question before opening the mark scheme.

Key ideas:
• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
• For the diver's motion in air, either use conservation of energy or resolve the initial velocity and use constant-acceleration equations.
• In water, identify every vertical force and choose a sign convention before applying F = ma.
• Drag depends on speed: as the diver slows, the drag force decreases.
• For the final acceleration, calculate the resultant force first, then divide by mass. State the direction as well as the magnitude.

Use the Official Mark Scheme tab to see exactly which intermediate steps and statements Cambridge awards marks for.

This question links stress, strain, Young modulus and elastic energy.

Useful route:
1. Read the stress corresponding to the stated strain from the graph.
2. Use stress = force / cross-sectional area, with A = πd²/4.
3. Young modulus is stress / strain in the linear elastic region.
4. For elastic energy, use the area under the force-extension graph (or 1/2 Fx when appropriate).

Be especially careful to convert mm to m and GPa to Pa. Compare your numerical working with the Official Mark Scheme to see where Cambridge places C/A marks.

Treat upward as positive and keep the sign convention consistent.

The ball initially moves upward, slows under the constant downward acceleration g, reaches v = 0 at its highest point, then accelerates downward. Constant-acceleration equations connect displacement, velocity and time.

For the graph part, use the physics rather than drawing by appearance: with negligible air resistance the acceleration is constant, so a velocity-time graph must have constant gradient.

Start by defining the system and a positive direction.

For the collision:
• total momentum before = total momentum after;
• include velocity signs, not just speeds;
• solve for the unknown velocity.

To decide whether a collision is perfectly elastic, compare total kinetic energy before and after. Momentum conservation alone does NOT establish that a collision is elastic.

The Official Mark Scheme shows the exact statements/calculations needed for each mark.

Choose the boat+sack as the system during the short collision.

1. State conservation of momentum correctly: total momentum of an isolated system remains constant.
2. Write momentum before = momentum after, including both masses in the final combined mass because the sack remains attached.
3. For the energy comparison, calculate total kinetic energy before and after separately.
4. If kinetic energy decreases, the collision is inelastic even though momentum is conserved.

Keep momentum (kg m s⁻¹) distinct from kinetic energy (J).

Use the wave definitions precisely.

Period is the time for one complete oscillation at a point. Frequency and period satisfy f = 1/T. Wave speed, frequency and wavelength satisfy v = fλ.

For diffraction/interference parts, identify the relevant path/wavelength condition before substituting numbers. Keep angles and orders clearly labelled, and use SI units for wavelength when calculating.

First law; series power; LDR potential divider
explanation: Start with Kirchhoff's first law: current entering a junction equals current leaving it. For the two series resistors, the current is the same, so compare powers using P=I^2 R. For the LDR circuit use I=5.4/1800=0.0030 A. The LDR has 9.0-5.4=3.6 V across it, giving R_L=3.6/0.0030=1200 ohm. As illumination increases, R_L falls, total resistance falls, current rises and the voltage across the fixed resistor increases.

solution_steps.title: Kirchhoff's first law
solution_steps.body: At any junction, the sum of currents entering equals the sum leaving: \(\sum I_{\mathrm{in}}=\sum I_{\mathrm{out}}\). This expresses conservation of charge.

solution_steps.title: The two resistors X and Y are in parallel
solution_steps.body: Parallel components have the same potential difference. Hence \(P=V^2/R\); since \(R_X>R_Y\), resistor **Y** dissipates more power. From \(R=\rho L/A\) (same material and length), **Y** also has the larger cross-sectional area.

solution_steps.title: Current and LDR resistance
solution_steps.body: \(I=5.4/1800=3.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm A\). Across the LDR, \(V_L=9.0-5.4=3.6\,\mathrm V\); therefore \(R_L=3.6/(3.0\times10^{-3})=\boxed{1200\,\Omega}\).

solution_steps.title: Effect of brighter light
solution_steps.body: The resistance of the LDR decreases. Series resistance decreases, so the circuit current rises. The p.d. across the fixed resistor \(V=I\times1800\) consequently increases.

topic: Kirchhoff voltage law; switching a resistor network
explanation: Apply Kirchhoff's second law to a closed loop: sum of electromotive forces equals sum of potential differences. Identify which resistors share current (series) and which share a potential difference (parallel). Compare the switch-open and switch-closed circuits by redrawing each configuration before applying V=IR.

solution_steps.title: Loop law
solution_steps.body: Write \(\sum\mathcal E=\sum IR\) around a closed loop; the signs must follow your chosen direction.

solution_steps.title: Switch-open case
solution_steps.body: Trace the actual conducting branches in Fig. 6.1 and redraw the active network. Decide which resistors have common current and which have common p.d. before applying \(V=IR\).

solution_steps.title: Switch-closed case
solution_steps.body: Repeat with the switch closed, checking whether a branch is bypassed. Apply both \(I_\mathrm{in}=I_\mathrm{out}\) and the loop rule if the circuit has a junction.

solution_steps.title: Self-check
solution_steps.body: Compare both arrangements against the Cambridge mark scheme; explain the physical reason for any changed currents or p.d.s.

topic: Kirchhoff current law; series resistance and internal resistance
explanation: Kirchhoff's first law expresses conservation of charge. For two series resistors the loop law gives V=V_1+V_2=I(R_1+R_2), so R_T=R_1+R_2. Here I=1.35/(10+15)=0.054 A and the lost volts are 1.50-1.35=0.15 V. Therefore r=0.15/0.054≈2.8 ohm. When R_3 is added in the configuration shown, reconsider the external equivalent resistance before judging the cell current and terminal p.d.

solution_steps.title: First law
solution_steps.body: \(\sum I_{\mathrm{in}}=\sum I_{\mathrm{out}}\). No charge accumulates at a junction in the steady state.

solution_steps.title: Derive the series rule
solution_steps.body: Using the loop law, \(V=V_1+V_2\). Since the current \(I\) is the same in each series resistor, \(IR_T=IR_1+IR_2\), hence \(\boxed{R_T=R_1+R_2}\).

solution_steps.title: Calculate internal resistance
solution_steps.body: \(I=1.35/(10+15)=0.054\,\mathrm A\). Lost volts: \(E-V=1.50-1.35=0.15\,\mathrm V\). Hence \(r=(E-V)/I=0.15/0.054=\boxed{2.8\,\Omega}\) to two significant figures.

solution_steps.title: Adding the extra resistor
solution_steps.body: The external equivalent resistance decreases, so current from the cell **increases**. Because the cell has internal resistance, \(Ir\) increases and the terminal p.d. \(V=E-Ir\) **decreases**.

topic: Kirchhoff second law; variable resistor and thermistor
explanation: Use the second law around the series loop: E=V_X+V_Y. For part (b)(i), V_X=9.0-4.0=5.0 V. Hence R_X=5.0/(1.1×10^-2)≈455 ohm. To find the new p.d. of Y, read its resistance at 190 Celsius from the graph, calculate I=9.0/(R_X+R_Y), then V_Y=IR_Y. Increasing R_X reduces the series current, so V_Y decreases when R_Y remains fixed.

solution_steps.title: Kirchhoff's second law
solution_steps.body: For any closed loop, the algebraic sum of electromotive forces equals the sum of potential differences. Equivalently, \(\sum\Delta V=0\).

solution_steps.title: Calculate the resistance of X
solution_steps.body: The components are in series: \(V_X=9.0-4.0=5.0\,\mathrm V\). Thus \(R_X=V_X/I=5.0/(1.1\times10^{-2})\approx\boxed{450\,\Omega}\), consistent with the official rounded result.

solution_steps.title: Read the graph and find the new p.d.
solution_steps.body: At \(190\,^\circ\mathrm C\), read \(R_Y\approx25\,\Omega\). Use the potential-divider relationship \(V_Y=E\,R_Y/(R_X+R_Y)=9.0(25)/(450+25)=\boxed{0.47\,\mathrm V}\).

solution_steps.title: Explain the final change
solution_steps.body: Increasing \(R_X\) increases total series resistance, so current falls. Since \(R_Y\) is constant at that temperature, \(V_Y=IR_Y\) **decreases**.

topic: Kirchhoff laws; parallel resistance and cell internal resistance
explanation: The second law is conservation of energy around a loop. For the parallel resistors, first law gives I=I_1+I_2 and both branches have the same p.d., V. Using I=V/R_T, I_1=V/R_1 and I_2=V/R_2 yields 1/R_T=1/R_1+1/R_2. For the numerical parts use E=I(R_T+r) and terminal p.d. V=E-Ir. Adding a parallel resistor reduces R_T, increases the cell current, and (for nonzero r) decreases terminal p.d.

solution_steps.title: State the second law
solution_steps.body: The sum of electromotive forces around a closed loop equals the sum of potential differences; it follows from conservation of energy.

solution_steps.title: Parallel combination proof
solution_steps.body: At the junction, \(I=I_1+I_2\) (first law). The p.d. is common to each parallel branch: \(V=IR_T=I_1R_1=I_2R_2\). Substituting currents gives \(\boxed{1/R_T=1/R_1+1/R_2}\).

solution_steps.title: Cell with internal resistance
solution_steps.body: Calculate \(R_T\) for the external parallel combination. Then use \(E=I(R_T+r)\) and \(V=E-Ir\) as required.

solution_steps.title: Adding a further parallel branch
solution_steps.body: Equivalent external resistance decreases; the current through the cell increases. Because the cell loses more volts internally (\(Ir\)), its terminal p.d. **decreases**.

topic: Kirchhoff second law; cells in parallel and resistance
explanation: For three identical cells in parallel, the equivalent electromotive force remains 1.5 V while the effective internal resistance is 0.590/3≈0.197 ohm. Since the total circuit resistance is 2.2 ohm, external resistance is ≈2.0 ohm. Current is I=1.5/2.2≈0.682 A. For cylindrical sections of equal length and material, R=ρL/A so the resistance ratio is the inverse area ratio. For drift speed, I=nAvq; identical current means drift speed is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.

solution_steps.title: Second law
solution_steps.body: The sum of electromotive forces equals the sum of potential differences around a closed loop.

solution_steps.title: Cells in parallel
solution_steps.body: For three identical cells in parallel, their net e.m.f. remains \(1.5\,\mathrm V\) and internal resistances are in parallel: \(r_\mathrm{eq}=0.590/3=0.197\,\Omega\).

solution_steps.title: External conductor resistance and current
solution_steps.body: Total resistance \(2.2\,\Omega\) includes internal resistance. Thus \(R_\mathrm{conductor}=2.2-0.197\approx\boxed{2.0\,\Omega}\). Then \(I=E/R_\mathrm{total}=1.5/2.2\approx\boxed{0.68\,\mathrm A}\).

solution_steps.title: Geometric ratios
solution_steps.body: For the same material and length, \(R\propto1/A\propto1/d^2\), so \(R_A/R_B=(d_B/d_A)^2=(7.6/4.3)^2\approx3.1\). Since current in A and B is equal, \(v\propto1/A\), giving the same ratio for \(v_A/v_B\).

topic: Kirchhoff first law; thermistor and internal resistance
explanation: At a junction, incoming current equals outgoing current. A negative-temperature-coefficient thermistor has falling resistance as temperature increases. Analyse which branches are in parallel and which elements are in series, then use the first law for the current split. For the cell, terminal p.d. is V=E-Ir. If the cell current grows, the lost volts Ir grow and the terminal p.d. falls.

solution_steps.title: The first law
solution_steps.body: At a junction, total incoming current equals total outgoing current.

solution_steps.title: Negative-temperature-coefficient thermistor
solution_steps.body: As temperature rises, its resistance falls; sketch a decreasing, curved resistance–temperature graph starting at \(R_0\).

solution_steps.title: Analyse the circuit
solution_steps.body: Redraw the current paths and identify series and parallel parts before calculating. Apply \(I_\mathrm{in}=\sum I_\mathrm{out}\) at junctions and \(V=IR\) in each branch.

solution_steps.title: Include internal resistance
solution_steps.body: Terminal potential difference is \(V=E-Ir\). Evaluate how the cell current changes when thermistor resistance drops, then how \(Ir\) and \(V\) change.

topic: Kirchhoff first law; LDR branches and terminal potential difference
explanation: Kirchhoff first law: total battery current equals the sum of branch currents. The terminal p.d. is V=E-Ir=5.0-(0.038)(4.7)=4.82 V, hence about 4.8 V. Use the resistor X current I_1=V/100, then Kirchhoff's law to determine I_2 with the actual branch arrangement shown in Fig. 5.1. For the power of Y, use P=I_2²R_Y. Decreasing incident light increases the LDR resistance, changing the total current and therefore the lost volts Ir.

solution_steps.title: First law
solution_steps.body: At a junction, the sum of currents entering equals the sum of currents leaving: \(\sum I_\mathrm{in}=\sum I_\mathrm{out}\).

solution_steps.title: Terminal p.d. of the battery
solution_steps.body: \(V=E-Ir=5.0-(38\times10^{-3})(4.7)=4.8214\,\mathrm V\approx\boxed{4.8\,\mathrm V}\).

solution_steps.title: Split of current between branches
solution_steps.body: Read \(R_Z=120\,\Omega\) from the graph. The branch containing X and Z has current \(I_1=4.8/(100+120)\approx0.022\,\mathrm A\). From Kirchhoff's first law, \(I_2=0.038-I_1\approx\boxed{0.016\,\mathrm A}\).

solution_steps.title: Power in resistor Y
solution_steps.body: \(P_Y=I_2V\approx0.016\times4.8=\boxed{0.077\,\mathrm W}\).

solution_steps.title: Reducing illumination
solution_steps.body: The LDR resistance rises; battery current falls. Thus the internal voltage loss \(Ir\) falls and terminal p.d. \(V=E-Ir\) **increases**.

topic: Kirchhoff loop rule; series and parallel resistors with internal resistance
explanation: Use Kirchhoff's second law: E=I(R_ext+r) for the cell. In series, R_ext=R_1+R_2; in parallel, 1/R_ext=1/R_1+1/R_2. In each circuit compute the new total resistance before calculating current. Remember that adding a parallel path decreases equivalent external resistance, but a real cell also has internal resistance.

solution_steps.title: Series circuit
solution_steps.body: Use the loop rule \(E=I(R_1+R_2+r)\). The cell's internal resistance \(r\) must be included in the total.

solution_steps.title: Parallel circuit
solution_steps.body: Once the two external resistors are reconnected in parallel, use \(R_\mathrm{ext}=R_1R_2/(R_1+R_2)\), followed by \(I=E/(R_\mathrm{ext}+r)\).

solution_steps.title: Compare cell currents
solution_steps.body: The external equivalent resistance decreases in the parallel arrangement, so cell current rises. Follow the original circuit diagram carefully when describing the new branch currents.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The rope pulls both the child and the sledge towards the pole with 12 N. Their common acceleration is \(a=24/(20+40)=0.40\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). The child needs a resultant of \(20a=8.0\ \mathrm N\), so friction on the child is 4.0 N away from the pole. Its magnitude is 4.0 N, A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Both spheres initially accelerate at approximately \(g\), since drag initially vanishes. The heavier stone needs a larger drag force to balance its weight, so its terminal speed is greater. Graph B shows the same initial gradient and the higher final speed for S.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For an elastic head-on collision, speed of separation equals speed of approach, \(5+15=20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Taking right as positive, \(7-v_X=20\), so \(v_X=-13\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\): 13 m/s to the left, B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: A couple consists of two equal, parallel forces acting in opposite directions along different lines of action. The resultant force is zero but the turning effect is non-zero. Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Taking moments about the hinge gives an upward tension component equal to half the rod's weight. Vertical equilibrium therefore requires the hinge to supply the other half upwards. It must also balance the tension's leftward component by acting rightwards. The hinge force points up and right, D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Use the additional moments due to the child: \(F_s\times2.0=40\times9.81\times5.0\), giving \(F_s=981\ \mathrm N\). The extra compression is \(x=F_s/k=981/10000=0.0981\ \mathrm m=9.8\ \mathrm{cm}\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Density is mass per unit volume, \(\rho=m/V\). Changing the gravitational field changes the rock's weight, but not its mass or, under the stated conditions, its volume. Its density remains \(\rho\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Pressures at the same horizontal level in the connected stationary liquid are equal. The liquid surfaces differ in height by \(y-z\), giving \(p_1-p_2=\rho g(y-z)\), C. Use the difference in liquid levels, not the full depth of either arm.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Power is work per unit time. Since \(W=Fs\), \(P=F(s/t)=Fv\) for force parallel to velocity. Force times velocity therefore has units of watts, B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: At fixed useful output, input power is inversely proportional to efficiency. Thus \(P_{new}/P_{old}=0.050/0.40=0.125\approx0.13\), A. The more efficient lamp needs less input power.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For the stated constant force, \(E_k=W=Fs\). Combining \(F=ma\) with \(v^2=2as\) gives \(E_k=\tfrac12mv^2\). The equation \(E=\tfrac12Fs\) is not needed and is not the work done by a constant force over displacement \(s\). Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: From \(E=FL/(Ax)\), the spring constant is \(k=F/x=EA/L\). Use \(A=\pi d^2/4\): \(k=2.0\times10^{11}\times\pi(0.48\times10^{-3})^2/(4\times1.6)\approx2.3\times10^4\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Beyond the elastic limit, unloading leaves permanent deformation, so plastic deformation has occurred. Proportionality of extension and force ends at the proportional limit, which need not equal the elastic limit. Hence A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Every progressive wave transfers energy from one place to another without a net transfer of the medium. Electromagnetic waves need no vibrating atoms, and ripple tanks demonstrate water waves rather than every wave type. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: In one oscillation the ball travels a vertical distance \(4A\). In 20 s it makes \(ft=0.20\times20=4\) oscillations. Total distance is \(4\times4\times0.70=11.2\ \mathrm m\), C. The horizontal wavelength does not determine the ball's vertical path length.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Lowest pressure occurs at the centre of a rarefaction, where neighbouring particles are displaced apart. On the displacement–distance graph this is the zero crossing with the largest positive gradient, point D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For the stationary observer, the source must move with a component of velocity towards or away from the observer. This changes the spacing of successive wavefronts reaching the observer. A change of emitted amplitude or frequency is not required. Hence A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The wavelength is \(\lambda=c/f=3.00\times10^8/(2.5\times10^{14})=1.2\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm m\), or 1.2 micrometres. This lies in the infrared region, A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Apply Malus' law at both filters. The first angle is 50 degrees to the incident polarisation; the second is 30 degrees to the new polarisation. \(I=8.0\cos^2 50^\circ\cos^2 30^\circ\approx2.5\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Neighbouring loops of a stationary wave oscillate in antiphase. Q and S are in loops separated by two nodes, so they oscillate in phase. R is an antinode and PT spans three half-wavelengths. Hence B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Diffraction is least when wavelength divided by gap width is smallest. Doubling frequency halves wavelength, and doubling the gap width gives a ratio one quarter of the original. Therefore D produces the smallest diffraction angle.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The strongest sound occurs where waves arrive in phase and their displacements reinforce. In the diagram, D lies at an intersection of wavefronts from the two speakers. This gives constructive interference; at destructive positions the amplitudes cancel.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: In \(d\sin\theta=n\lambda\), \(n\) is the order of the intensity maximum and \(d\) is the distance between adjacent slits. It is not the distance to the screen. Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The number of charge carriers in the block is \(nV\), so their total charge magnitude is \(nqV\). They pass through in average time \(t\), giving \(I=Q/t=nqV/t\), B. Equivalently use \(I=nqAv\) with \(v=L/t\) and \(AL=V\).

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Use \(P=I^2R\): \(P_X/P_Y=(0.50^2\times9.6)/(3.0^2\times1.2)=2.4/10.8\approx0.22\), A. Neither the currents nor the resistances alone determine the power ratio.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: More light reduces the LDR's resistance; a higher temperature reduces the resistance of the NTC thermistor used here. With current fixed, \(V=IR\), so the potential difference decreases for both components, D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For the same material at the same temperature, \(R\propto L/d^2\). The second wire has one quarter the length and twice the diameter, so \(R_2/R=(2/8)(0.50/1.0)^2=1/16\), A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The current is \(I=\mathcal E/(R+r)\), so increasing internal resistance reduces current. The terminal p.d. across the fixed external resistor is \(V=IR\) and therefore decreases. Hence B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Kirchhoff's first law expresses conservation of charge at a junction. The second law expresses conservation of energy around a closed loop. The correct pairing is charge / energy, A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The known cell must drive current through the uniform potentiometer wire. The unknown cell is connected with polarity opposing the potential difference along the balance length, so the galvanometer can read zero. Circuit D satisfies these conditions; at balance no current is drawn from the unknown cell.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Scattering shows that atoms are mostly empty space and contain a very small, dense, positively charged nucleus. It does not identify protons as its constituents. Statement C cannot be deduced from this experiment alone.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Neutron absorption increases mass number by 1 without changing proton number. Subsequent alpha emission reduces mass number by 4 and proton number by 2: \(^{28}_{14}E\to{}^{29}_{14}E\to{}^{25}_{12}M\). Thus C. Isotopes must share proton number, not mass number.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Beta-minus decay changes a neutron into a proton: one down quark becomes an up quark, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. \(d\to u+e^-+\bar\nu_e\), B. Charge is conserved: \(-1/3=2/3-1\).

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs, not amperes. The ampere measures electric current, \(I=Q/t\). A gram is a valid unit of mass even though the SI base unit is the kilogram. Hence C is the incorrect pairing.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For a small car of mass roughly \(1000\ \mathrm{kg}\) travelling at about \(10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), \(E_k=\tfrac12mv^2\approx5\times10^4\ \mathrm J\). This gives the reasonable order of magnitude A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For a square cross-section, \(V=Lw^2\). Add fractional uncertainties with the power of each quantity: \(100\Delta V/V=100(0.2/50.0)+2\times100(0.01/2.00)=0.4+1.0=1.4\%\), D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Acceleration is the gradient of the velocity–time graph. The positive acceleration first increases then falls to zero, so velocity rises throughout, with an initially increasing and then decreasing gradient, finishing horizontal. Graph A has this shape.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Use \(v^2=u^2+2gs\) with \(u=0\): \(v=\sqrt{2\times9.81\times0.40}=2.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), B. Falling distance cannot be substituted for time in \(v=gt\).

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: With air resistance negligible, gravity provides a constant downward acceleration throughout the flight. The path is parabolic, and the time to fall depends on the vertical motion rather than the horizontal launch speed. Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Momentum is conserved in the isolated system, while kinetic energy decreases when the objects stick together. Row C has unchanged momentum and a reduction in kinetic energy; rows B and D contradict the stated inelastic collision.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: At terminal velocity, speed is constant and acceleration is zero. Height above the ground therefore decreases linearly with time. The downward-sloping straight line represents height against time, B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The velocity reverses, so the momentum-change magnitude is \(m(u+v)=2.0(4.0+2.8)=13.6\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}\). Average force is \(13.6/0.150\approx91\ \mathrm N\), D. The wall experiences the equal and opposite force.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Taking the first carriage's direction as positive, conservation of momentum gives \(v=(5000\times2.00-5000\times1.00)/10000=0.50\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Initial kinetic energy is 12500 J and final kinetic energy is 1250 J. The loss is 11250 J, C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: An object in equilibrium has zero resultant force, so no translational acceleration. It may be stationary or moving at constant velocity, and individual forces may still act. Hence D is necessary. For an extended body, rotational equilibrium also requires zero resultant moment.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: In equilibrium the three force vectors must form a closed head-to-tail triangle. Weight points downwards, tension pulls the kite along the string towards its anchor, and the wind force balances their resultant. Diagram A gives those directions and closes the triangle.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The two 6.0 N forces form a clockwise couple with separation \(7.0+3.0=10.0\ \mathrm m\), giving 60 N m. The opposing 5.0 N couple has perpendicular separation \(XY\sin60^\circ\). Thus \(5.0\,XY\sin60^\circ=60\), so \(XY\approx14\ \mathrm m\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Maximum pressure occurs on the smallest face, so the vertical height is the largest dimension, 0.150 m. Using \(p=mg/A=\rho gh\), \(p=1.13\times10^4\times9.81\times0.150\approx16.6\ \mathrm{kPa}\), D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, \(P=\Delta W/\Delta t\): work done per unit time. The word 'per' expresses the required division. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Useful mechanical power is \(0.60\times800=480\ \mathrm W\). At constant velocity, driving force equals the total resistive force. From \(P=Fv\), \(F=480/12=40\ \mathrm N\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Energy can be transferred between stores or transformed between forms, but total energy in a closed system remains constant. Useful output alone can be smaller than input because some energy is dissipated. Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: With no friction and no required gain of kinetic energy, minimum work equals the gain in gravitational potential energy: \(W=mgh=50\times9.81\times1.6\approx780\ \mathrm J\), C. The plank length affects the required force, not this energy increase.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Stress is force divided by area, with unit \(\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}\). Since \(1\ \mathrm N=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}\), the base-unit form is \(\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}\,s^{-2}}\), A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Young modulus is the gradient of a stress–strain graph in its linear region. P has approximately twice Q's gradient, so at equal stress P has about half Q's strain and extension, not twice. R is approximately linear below strain 0.1. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Each rod supports one quarter of the total force: \(F=2500\ \mathrm N\). With \(A=250\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^2}\) and \(x=0.10\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm m\), \(E=FL/(Ax)=2.0\times10^{11}\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Work done is \(\tfrac12F\Delta L\) for a Hooke's-law spring. The graph plots total length against force, so its non-zero initial length must not be included as extension. The triangle labelled P equals \(\tfrac12F\Delta L\), giving A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Amplitude is the component along the transmission axis: \(A_{out}=A\cos50^\circ\approx0.64A\), C. The squared cosine applies to intensity, which is proportional to amplitude squared, not to amplitude itself.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: P and Q are centres of successive rarefactions, one wavelength apart. At a rarefaction centre the displacement is zero with positive spatial gradient. The graph must therefore start and end at zero with positive gradient and complete one cycle: C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The wavelength is \(c/f=1.0\times10^{-8}\ \mathrm m\), in the ultraviolet region at this boundary convention. Visible light has a lower frequency than this ultraviolet wave, whereas X-rays have higher frequencies. Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: A source moving away produces a lower observed frequency, \(f_o=f_sv/(v+v_s)\). A greater recession speed lowers it further. Of the choices, 10 m/s away gives the lowest frequency, B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The time-base specifies the time represented by one horizontal division of the CRO screen, for example milliseconds per division. Multiply it by the divisions in one cycle to find the period. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The principle of superposition states that the resultant displacement is the algebraic sum of the individual displacements at that point and instant. Signs or phases matter; the amplitudes cannot simply always be added. Hence B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The angular spread decreases as \(\lambda/a\) decreases. Reducing period increases frequency and reduces wavelength, since \(\lambda=cT\). With slit width fixed, this reduces diffraction, B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Use the fourth-order maximum in \(d\sin\theta=n\lambda\): \(\lambda=(2.7\times10^{-6})\sin53^\circ/4=5.4\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm m\), B. The order number is 4, not the number of lines in the grating.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Dust gathers at displacement nodes. Four heaps span three node-to-node intervals, so \(3\lambda/2=0.30\ \mathrm m\), giving \(\lambda=0.20\ \mathrm m\). Then \(f=v/\lambda=330/0.20=1650\ \mathrm{Hz}\), A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Electric charge is quantised. In a metal the charge transferred by individual electrons is an integer multiple of the elementary charge, \(Q=Ne\). Current is the rate of charge flow, not the charge itself. Hence B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: As the filament heats up, its resistance increases. Current still rises with potential difference, but the I–V curve becomes less steep as voltage increases. Graph A has this behaviour; the lamp is not ohmic over this range.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: An electron's average traversal time is \(t=L/v=0.35/(5.0\times10^{-4})=700\ \mathrm s\). In that time \(Q=It=8400\ \mathrm C\) passes, so \(N=Q/e=8400/(1.60\times10^{-19})=5.3\times10^{22}\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: In circuit B, the two 100-ohm resistors are in parallel, giving 50 ohms. This combination is in series with the other 50-ohm resistor, making \(R_{total}=50+50=100\ \Omega\).

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Kirchhoff's first law follows from conservation of charge at junctions. The second follows from conservation of energy around a complete circuit loop. Hence A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Using \(\mathcal E=I(R+r)\), \(r=\mathcal E/I-R=1.50/0.26-5.0\approx0.77\ \Omega\), D. The terminal p.d. is \(IR=1.30\ \mathrm V\); the remaining 0.20 V is across the internal resistance.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: A meson is a composite particle made of a quark and an antiquark, not a quark flavour. Up, strange and charm are all quark flavours. Hence B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Hydrogen-3 has one proton and two neutrons. A proton (uud) contains one down quark; a neutron (udd) contains two. The total is \(1+2\times2=5\) down quarks, D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: In beta-plus decay, \(p\to n+e^++\nu_e\). An electron neutrino is emitted along with the positron to conserve lepton number. Beta-minus decay instead emits an electron antineutrino. Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Work is a scalar: it has no associated direction, even though the force and displacement used to calculate it are vectors. Force, momentum and velocity are vector quantities. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: A systematic error introduces a consistent bias relative to the correct value and therefore reduces accuracy. It is not the random scatter between repeated readings. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Read the change in velocity, not the final value: \(\Delta v=150-30=120\ \mathrm{cm\,s^{-1}}=1.20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Thus \(a=1.20/5.0=0.24\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) and \(m=F/a=300/0.24=1250\ \mathrm{kg}\approx1300\ \mathrm{kg}\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Convert \(85\ \mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}\) to \(23.6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and use the maximum available distance, 1200 m. From \(v^2=2as\), \(a=v^2/(2s)=0.23\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\), A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Horizontal velocity remains \(20\cos45^\circ\), so the speed is non-zero even at the highest point, where vertical velocity is zero. On returning to its original height, conservation of energy gives the original speed of 20 m/s. Hence A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Total momentum of a system is conserved when no resultant external force acts on it. This applies to inelastic as well as elastic collisions; kinetic energy need not be conserved. Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Conserve momentum in P's original direction. Q's component is opposite to P's, so \(p_x=6.0\times3.0-2.0\times4.2\cos35^\circ=11.1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}\). The final combined momentum has the same component, approximately 11 kg m/s, B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The gravitational force remains \(mg\) at launch. The upward acceleration requires a support force larger than the weight, but does not itself change the gravitational field or mass. Hence B; \(1.2mg\) would be the support force.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For a uniform plank, its weight can be represented as acting at its midpoint. Since the pivot is there, the plank's own weight has zero moment about it. The pivot also supports the children, so its force exceeds the plank's weight. Hence A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For a fully submerged object, \(U=\rho_{liquid}gV\) and \(W=\rho_{object}gV\), so \(U/W=\rho_{liquid}/\rho_{object}\). Doubling liquid density doubles this ratio; changing object volume alone cancels out. Hence A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The angled rod must supply an upward component of 75 N. If its force magnitude is \(T\), \(T\sin30^\circ=75\), so \(T=150\ \mathrm N\). The horizontal reaction is \(T\cos30^\circ\approx130\ \mathrm N\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Density is \(\rho=4m/(\pi d^2h)\). Add percentage uncertainties, counting the diameter twice: \(10+2(3)+2=18\%\), D. The numerical constants contribute no uncertainty.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The uniform plank alone contributes 150 N to each support. When the child stands at X, the full additional 600 N acts on X, giving 750 N there. At Y, the additional 600 N is supported at Y, leaving 150 N at X. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: From \(P=W/t\) and \(W=Fs\), use \(s=vt\) to obtain \(P=Fvt/t=Fv\). This assumes the force component parallel to the velocity. Hence A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The vertical drop is \(h=L\sin\theta\). With no resistive forces, \(mgL\sin\theta=\tfrac12mv^2\). Thus \(v=\sqrt{2gL\sin\theta}=4.43\sqrt{L\sin\theta}\) in SI units, B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Work done by a force parallel to displacement is \(W=Fs\). Here \(W=25\times0.50=12.5\ \mathrm J\approx13\ \mathrm J\), A. The mass is not needed for this calculation.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The mass flow rate is \(\dot m=1000\times340/60\ \mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}}\). Useful power is \(P=0.90\dot mgh=0.90(1000\times340/60)9.81\times30\approx1.5\ \mathrm{MW}\), B. Convert minutes to seconds.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: At maximum height only the unchanged horizontal velocity remains. Therefore \(E_{top}/E=(u\cos45^\circ)^2/u^2=\cos^2 45^\circ=0.50\). Hence A; velocity components must be squared when comparing kinetic energies.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Elastic deformation means the original length is recovered when the force is removed. It does not necessarily mean extension is proportional to force: that is the additional condition of Hooke's law. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The tensile force is the same through both sections. Stress \(F/A\) is inversely proportional to diameter squared, so \(\sigma_Y/\sigma_X=(2d/d)^2=4\), D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Each spring supports 40 N. The graph gives a compression of about 2.4 mm at this force. Total energy is \(4\times\tfrac12\times40\times2.4\times10^{-3}=0.192\ \mathrm J\approx0.19\ \mathrm J\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: All electromagnetic waves are transverse and can propagate through free space. They are not longitudinal waves. Row A gives this combination.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Infrared wavelengths are longer than visible red and extend to about 1 mm. The approximate range 800 nm to 1000 micrometres is therefore the infrared range among these choices, D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The car recedes from P and approaches Q at constant speed along their line. P hears a constant lower frequency and Q a constant higher frequency. Neither frequency gradually changes during this segment; only statement 3 is correct, C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The wavelength is \(\lambda=v/f=600/300=2.0\ \mathrm m\). A separation of 0.50 m is one quarter of a wavelength, giving \(\Delta\phi=360^\circ(0.50/2.0)=90^\circ\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Initially the filter is aligned with the incident polarisation because the transmitted intensity is unchanged. After rotation, \(I_{out}/I=\cos^2\theta=0.75\). Thus \(\theta=30^\circ\), A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Stable observable interference requires coherence: the waves have a constant phase difference and the same frequency. Equal amplitudes improve contrast but are not necessary for interference. Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Diffraction increases when the ratio of wavelength to gap width increases. Increasing wavelength while decreasing the gap width guarantees an increase in this ratio. Hence C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Grating spacing is \(d=1/(400\times10^3)=2.50\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm m\). Use \(\sin\theta_n=n\lambda/d\): \(\theta_2\approx26.97^\circ\), \(\theta_3\approx42.88^\circ\). Their difference is 15.9 degrees, C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Series conductors carry the same current, so the same number of charge carriers passes each per unit time. From \(I=nqAv\), the smaller area in Y requires a greater average drift speed for the same material. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Use \(R=\rho L/A\) and \(A=\pi d^2/4\). Then \(d=\sqrt{4\rho L/(\pi R)}=\sqrt{4(1.8\times10^{-8})(6.4)/(\pi\times0.92)}\approx4.0\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm m\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: An NTC thermistor's resistance falls as temperature rises. The ideal cell fixes the potential difference, so \(P=V^2/R\) increases, rather than decreasing or remaining constant. The increasing curved graph A matches this behaviour.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Charge transferred in one minute is \(Q=It=(V/R)t\). Thus \(N=Q/e=9.0\times60/(5.6\times10^3\times1.60\times10^{-19})\approx6.0\times10^{17}\), C. Convert kilohms to ohms and minutes to seconds.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Symbol B is a resistive heating element, whose intended output is thermal energy rather than sound. The other symbols represent sound-emitting devices. Hence B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Kirchhoff's first law gives a current of 2 A in R: the 3 A current is balanced by 1 A in P and 2 A in R, using the arrows shown. Then \(Q=It=2\times5=10\ \mathrm C\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: With the switch open, current is zero and terminal p.d. equals the e.m.f. Closing the switch gives current through the internal resistance, producing lost volts \(Ir\). The terminal p.d. becomes \(V=E-Ir\) and decreases, B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: A baryon consists of three quarks. They can be different flavours, as in a proton (uud) or neutron (udd); they do not all have to be the same flavour. Hence B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Initial momentum is zero, so the emitted proton and daughter nucleus have equal and opposite momenta. Approximating their masses as \(m_p\) and \((A-1)m_p\), \(m_pv=(A-1)m_pu\), giving \(v=(A-1)u\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: In beta-plus decay a proton becomes a neutron. Its quark composition changes from uud to udd, so one up quark becomes a down quark. A positron and electron neutrino are emitted. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Charm belongs to the up-type quarks and has charge \(+\tfrac23e\), the same as an up quark. The corresponding antiquark has the opposite charge. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: A physical quantity must include a numerical value. Its value need not be an integer, and its unit need not be an SI unit or be expanded into base units. Hence C; recording the numerical value is necessary even when a different valid unit is used.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Use \(R=V/I=P/I^2\). Since \(\mathrm W=\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-3}}\), the ohm in SI base units is \(\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-3}\,A^{-2}}\), A. Options expressed using joules, coulombs or watts are not entirely in base units.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: X's reading is only 0.5 cm from the true value, compared with 1.4 cm for Y, so X is more accurate. X's stated uncertainty is larger (0.5 cm rather than 0.1 cm), so it is less precise. Hence D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Rearrange \(\mathbf X=\mathbf Y-\mathbf Z\) to \(\mathbf Z=\mathbf Y-\mathbf X\). Reverse X and add it to the rightward vector Y. The resultant points down and right, matching A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: By definition, constant acceleration is \(a=(v-u)/t\). Rearranging directly gives \(v=u+at\), C. The displacement equations require an additional relation involving displacement or average velocity.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For uniform vertical acceleration from zero initial vertical velocity, vertical displacement is \(s_y=\tfrac12at^2\): its graph starts with zero gradient and becomes progressively steeper. Graph D shows this. Uniform horizontal velocity would give a straight displacement–time graph.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The combined outlet area is \(A=400\times0.4\times10^{-6}=1.6\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2}\). Mass flow rate is \(\rho Av\), so the horizontal momentum flow rate is \(F=\rho Av^2=900(1.6\times10^{-4})(2.5)^2=0.90\ \mathrm N\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Newton's third-law forces act on different bodies in the same interaction. Earth's gravitational pull on the Moon and the Moon's pull on Earth form such a pair, B. Weight and support on one object are balanced forces, not a third-law pair.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For each ball, upward drag plus upthrust equals weight, so both have zero acceleration and are at terminal speed. Equal volume gives equal upthrust. The heavier ball needs greater drag to balance its weight, hence a greater terminal speed for the same shape and size, D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Total kinetic energy is conserved. X initially has \(\tfrac12mv^2\) and finally has \(\tfrac12m(3v/5)^2=9mv^2/50\). Y therefore gains \((25-9)mv^2/50=16mv^2/50\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For a couple the forces must have distinct parallel lines of action. If both acted through the same point, their equal and opposite forces would produce no turning effect. Acting through the same point is therefore not a requirement, B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The rule's weight acts at 50.0 cm. Balancing moments about 34.0 cm gives \(64g(34-4)=Mg(50-34)\), with masses expressed consistently in grams. Thus \(M=64\times30/16=120\ \mathrm g\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Add masses, not densities: \(m=1000\times1.5+800\times0.50=1900\ \mathrm{kg}\). Divide by the stated total volume: \(\rho=1900/2.0=950\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\), D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Archimedes' principle gives upthrust equal to the weight of displaced liquid, \(F_U=W_L\), A. At terminal speed, the object's weight is balanced by upthrust plus drag, so upthrust need not equal the object's weight.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Source ambiguity — excluded from new scored sessions. Do not use this item to judge mastery until its wording and intended interpretation have been reviewed.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: At constant speed, useful mechanical power is \(P_{out}=Fv\). Efficiency \(0.25=P_{out}/P_{in}\) gives \(P_{in}=4Fv\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Horizontal velocity is constant: \(u_x=18/1.5=12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). At the highest point vertical velocity is zero, so \(E_k=\tfrac12mu_x^2=\tfrac12\times0.40\times12^2=28.8\ \mathrm J\approx29\ \mathrm J\), D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: From \(E=FL/(Ax)\), \(F=EAx/L\). Use \(A=\pi(1.0\times10^{-3})^2/4\), \(E=360\times10^9\ \mathrm{Pa}\) and \(x=7.2\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm m\). This gives \(F\approx3.9\times10^2\ \mathrm N\), B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Work is the area under the force–extension graph. The extension is \(L_1-L_0\), so the triangular area is \(W=\tfrac12F(L_1-L_0)\), B. The original length does not contribute to the extension.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: First find \(\lambda=v/f=340/1500=0.2267\ \mathrm m\). The minimum separation is \(\Delta x=(70/360)\lambda=0.0441\ \mathrm m=4.4\ \mathrm{cm}\), A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The time graph gives a period of 0.40 s, while the distance graph gives a wavelength of 120 cm. Thus \(v=\lambda/T=120/0.40=300\ \mathrm{cm\,s^{-1}}\), D. Read a complete cycle on each graph.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The moving source compresses wavefronts ahead of it and spreads them behind it. The observed frequency changes from higher on approach to lower on recession: the Doppler effect, D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: A wavelength of 2.1 cm, or \(2.1\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm m\), lies in the microwave region of the electromagnetic spectrum. Hence B.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Initially both filter axes align with the source polarisation. After 90 degrees the first filter is crossed with the source, so no light is transmitted even though the two filters are mutually parallel. After 180 degrees both axes are equivalent to their initial directions. Thus darkest then brightest, C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: R is a node and remains undisplaced. S and T lie in adjacent loops of the stationary wave, so they oscillate in antiphase; immediately after the extreme position they move in opposite directions. Hence B. Antinodes in adjacent loops are half a wavelength apart.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Successive maxima on the plotted stationary-wave pattern are 10 cm apart, corresponding to \(\lambda/2\). Hence \(\lambda=0.20\ \mathrm m\) and \(f=v/\lambda=340/0.20=1700\ \mathrm{Hz}\), A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: The amount of diffraction depends on wavelength divided by gap width. To keep this ratio unchanged when wavelength doubles, double the gap width too: \(w_{new}=2w\), C.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Coherent waves have the same frequency and constant phase difference, and both electromagnetic waves travel at \(c\) in a vacuum. Since their intensities differ, their amplitudes differ because \(I\propto A^2\). Statement B is not correct.

mcq_explanation: In a metal, mobile conduction electrons carry charge while the positive ion lattice remains in place. Their average drift is from the cell's negative terminal towards its positive terminal, opposite to conventional current. Hence A.

mcq_explanation: Each parallel resistor has the full 12 V across it. Total power is \(36=12^2/R+12^2/(2R)=216/R\), giving \(R=6.0\ \Omega\), D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: For an NTC thermistor, resistance falls as temperature rises. The total series resistance therefore falls, and the current from the fixed-voltage cell rises non-linearly. Graph B shows this increase.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Current is charge transferred per unit time. Equality of currents entering and leaving a junction means charge is not accumulating there: conservation of charge, A.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: Proton number is nucleon number minus neutron number. P, Q, R and S have proton numbers 5, 4, 8 and 8 respectively. R and S therefore have the same proton number but different neutron numbers: they are isotopes, D.

explanation_review.author: AI-authored teaching commentary; teacher review welcome

mcq_explanation: In beta-minus decay, \(n\to p+e^-+\bar\nu_e\): a neutron becomes a proton and an electron and electron antineutrino are emitted. Hence A.
